book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.1: Look on the bright side: everyone in the world loves Vita more than her mother, Sa, does. If Vita annoys you, you can beat her up and tell her, "Even though I hit you, I still love you more than your mother does." What can she say? Go back and complain to Mommy Sa? Whenever Vita tries to show Sa affection, Sa's answer is: emotional neglect counts as a gift, being scolded to tears counts as a reward, and surviving a beating counts as hitting the jackpot. After so long without being treated as a person, Vita still distrusts any "love" even after leaving Sa to live alone. Only someone like Sparkle, who occasionally goes wild and literally fights her way into friendship, can become a true sister to her. From Kiana, Griseo, or Mei, even the occasional warmth slightly greater than that shown to a stranger is enough to make Vita resemble a stray puppy that accidentally ate chocolate: craving the sweetness left in its mouth while howling and convulsing in pain, then screaming as it flees back to its solitary little nest to curl up and tremble. Oh, sorry, I forgot — when did Vita ever have a home?
book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.2:
There is a Bud of Desire who has never hugged her own god.
Yes, that is Rice Cake, because Rice Cake has no hands; usually Kiana hugs Rice Cake.
There is a Bud of Desire whose god has never looked her in the eye.
Yes, that is "Prisoner Xun," because Xun and Lei are too busy looking at Sena to look at anyone else.
According to incomplete statistics, about 1/3 of gods have abandoned their Buds of Desire.
Three Buds feel pinned down while sleeping. Rice Cake opens her eyes to find Kiana hugging her in her sleep. Xun opens her eyes to find herself hugging Sena. Little Vita really is pinned down.
Rice Cake can crawl into anyone's bed, because everyone loves her. Xun can rest on either planet, because both sides accept her. Our little Vita is even more impressive: she can wander anywhere, wherever she wants to wander.
book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.3:
Vita is the best-behaved: she never runs away from home. Because she has no home.
Vita is the most obedient: she never causes trouble. Because there is no one left to talk to.
Vita is the freest: no one disciplines her. Because no one notices her and no one cares about her.
book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.4: Ordinary people cannot laugh too loudly at these late at night, because they might wake their family. Little V need not worry.
book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.5: We must imagine little Vita happy, because everyone loves her more than her mother does.
book.lastsongofelysian.ivtv.page.6: Sa tormented little Vita until she stopped trusting love. If someone genuinely shows her kindness, she becomes flustered and runs away at lightning speed. Only the little Vitas are exceptions, but they cannot remember her, leaving her rootless and wandering. Little Vita always wanted to be close to her creator. If Sa returned even a trace of kindness, Vita would devote her life to serving her. But Sa could not. When Sa died, little Vita was the saddest — and the only one who grieved.
